answer: One warden runs a single refuge hut on a mesa trail for 90 days, and travelers who wander past sign a dated log with name and destination. The warden pays a 120 dollar license fee and locks a 180 token deposit, photographs the meadow path weekly, and a ranger visits twice to match the log against footprints and weather notes. A forged log forfeits the deposit and bars the warden 180 days. Like a lighthouse log that must match each ship that passed, a warden's book must match real feet on the trail, so faking 10,000 huts would freeze 1,800,000 tokens and cost 1,200,000 dollars in fees.
